Report boosterpak project status

Source: R/status.R
status.Rd

Report boosterpak project status

Usage

status(root = ".", verbose = NULL)

Arguments

root

Project root.

verbose

Whether to print routine summaries.

Value

A list describing project status, invisibly. Includes config validity, declared and resolved packs, package and missing-package counts, attach state, materialized function drift/missing counts, pack catalog counts, selected package-library strategy and path, renv state, lockfile presence, and .Rprofile hook state.

The attach fields are attach_enabled; attach_packages, the names of every attached package, and attach_package_count, its length; and attach_every_start_count, the number of those packages attached on every R start, including workers. attach_interactive_packages names the packages attached only in interactive sessions (attach_mode = "interactive" packs). attach_sources is a data frame with one row per attached package and columns package, pack, and interactive. pack names the packs that requested the package, or "[attach].declared" for packages listed in boosters.toml. interactive is TRUE for interactive-only packages.

upgrade_needed is TRUE when boosters.toml exists and its boosters_version record is missing, unreadable, or older than the installed boosterpak. Only an older or unreadable record, or an earlier .Rprofile layout, prints a warning. A missing record is reported as "no version recorded" and prints no warning, because a project created with init(rprofile = "no") has none. A .Rprofile with no boosterpak hook is informational, not a warning. Run upgrade_project(dry_run = TRUE) before upgrade_project() when a warning asks for it.

github_token_visible is NA unless the project declares GitHub sources (owner/repo specifications from [extras].declared or from pack sources). Then it is TRUE when a token is visible through the GITHUB_PAT or GITHUB_TOKEN environment variables or, when the gitcreds package is installed, through its credential store. The token value is never returned or printed.
